_notes: The lamps are lit in the wrong order and the Lamplighters are nowhere. The rag-wraith is the lesson about declining a fight.
Scenes 12-17 of the prologue as it was before the split; `--scene story:<index>` still counts across the whole prologue, not within this file.

lines: That was when I noticed the quiet. No pigeons — and pigeons are never quiet. The roofline sat against the sky, empty as a shelf.
The lamps on Needle Lane are lit in the wrong order. You would have to live here to see it: third lamp, then first, then the one by the pump. The order is the stitch.
Tonight the lane reads dark-bright-dark-dark-bright — a signature forged by someone who has only ever seen it written. The dog at Number Twelve is awake, and does not bark.

Halfway down, the fog stops being fog. It has sleeves. It has a collar. It has the shape of a person who is not in it, and every cut thread on the street is sliding towards it like water finding a drain.

notes: ❋ GUILE, the green patience — and MOONLIGHT, which is hers. Moonlight is WILD: one Moonlight card pays for anything you own.

coach.text: Nothing was healed on the walk here. Your heart, your spool and every action's remaining uses carried straight over from the wisp — one night, one budget, all the way to the end of it.
A RAG-WRAITH: clothes whose owner is missing. Not dead — missing. It is above your weight, and it knows it. Ten years ago it would still have been above your weight.
Guile in hand, which is what the LOAF wants: block 5, but it costs your whole turn. A loaf is not a lunge.
PURR heals 2 a turn for two turns — but Ash lies still while it lasts, and it breaks the moment you are hit. Purr behind a guard, never in the open.
CONCENTRATE, for an empty hand: give up the turn to will one spent energy back. It arrives NEXT turn. Twice a fight.
And you do not have to win this. SLIP AWAY is a real answer — though it gets its telegraphed move in as you go.

lines: I went in with everything I had, and then with the pale cold weight under my ribs that is hers. I felt it go out of me and do nothing.
Three streets before I stopped, and I stopped because my legs decided it. It was not hunting me. It was WORKING, and I did not know yet at what.
It comes apart in the middle of the road and the threads go slack. That was above my weight and both of us knew it.
It was not hunting me. It was WORKING, and I did not know yet at what.
